newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen boss rushed to hospital in false alarm.
newsitem.headline: Chechen boss rushed to hospital in false alarm.

text.p: Chechen separatist leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev was rushed to hospital overnight but fears that he had apendicitis proved unfounded, his spokesman was quoted as saying on Monday.

Chief rebel spokesman Movladi Udugov told Itar-Tass news agency that doctors first suspected apendicitis but later established it was only food poisoning. Yandarbiyev felt well and was likely to resume working later on Monday.
Udugov did not say at which hospital Yandarbiyev was treated.
Yandarbiyev, a 44-year-old writer, took over the separatists' self-styled presidency in April after Dzhokhar Dudayev was reported killed in a rocket attack.

He had been expected in Moscow this week, possibly as early as Monday, for further talks on last month's peace settlement with Kremlin security chief Alexander Lebed and, perhaps, Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
Interfax news agency reported on Sunday, however, that Yandarbiyev would not travel until the end of the month to allow more time to prepare for the meetings.
Yandarbiyev last visited Moscow in May to sign a previous ceasefire deal with Boris Yeltsin, who was then fighting for re-election. That deal failed after Yeltsin won a second term.
The Russian president is now himself in hospital awaiting major heart surgery amid rumours that Lebed, Chernomyrdin and others are manoeuvring for power in his absence.
